request.what: Reduce the committeeMinSize protocol parameter from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal would reduce the minimum Constitutional Committee size, committeeMinSize, from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee has 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize setting of 7.

If Constitutional Committee membership drops below committeeMinSize, governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval become ineligible for ratification, including Parameter Changes, Constitution Updates, Treasury Withdrawals, and Hard Forks.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 is intended to create an operational buffer so governance can continue if one or two current members retire or have terms expire.

The proposal states that this action depends temporally on enactment of another live Parameter Change governance action for Plutus cost model settings, with no technical interaction between the two parameter changes.
The proposal states the change does not directly alter the current number of Constitutional Committee members or the maximum number of Constitutional Committee members.

The proposal acknowledges that at a committee size of 5, one inactive member would allow another member to fully veto governance actions under an assumed 2/3 Constitutional Committee voting threshold.
The proposal states the change underwent Parameter Committee technical review through PCP-005 and references a Cardano Forum discussion for that process.
The proposal states guardrails CMS-01, CMS-02, and CMS-03 are satisfied because committeeMinSize would be 5, which is nonnegative, not below 3, and not above 10.

The proposal states the change is reversible if at least 7 Constitutional Committee members exist, while reverting to 7 when fewer than 7 members exist would immediately halt governance until enough members were elected.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury parameter change to lower committeeMinSize from 7 to 5, arguing this improves governance continuity while disclosing threshold and veto implications, guardrail compliance, review references, dependency on another live action, and a conditional reversion plan.
